title: JFR: emit a large event if fails to write as an small event

timeline.message: JFR: Generate a large event if it does not fit into a small event
timeline.author: Jovan Stevanovic
Zhengyu Gu
Zhengyu Gu

timeline.body:
Please review this patch that upgrades an event to an large event if it is failed to be emitted as a small event.

The implementation mirrors Hotspot implementation, through a retry mechanism.

I only apply retry to various length events, e.g. events contain `string`. For fixed length (uncompressed) events that obviously fit small events, I elect to add assert to ensure they are properly emitted.
 
This patch also fixes #[3636](https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/3636)
Shouldn't `large` be `false` in this case? At the moment, there is a mismatch between the value used for `beginEventWrite` and `endEventWrite`.

I don't think that it is possible to assert that. It can happen that the event is cancelled (`JfrNativeEventWriter.cancel`) because flushing the thread-local buffer fails (e.g., if there isn't any remaining space in the global buffers).
`setLarge(JfrEvent event, boolean large)` is probably easier to use in the callers.

I think it is important to document this retry pattern and why it actually works (e.g., in the class-level JavaDoc of `JfrNativeEventWriter`): if the small event got cancelled (e.g., because the flushing fails), then the `JfrNativeEventWriterData` remains in the cancelled state and it is therefore guaranteed that retry fails as well. So, the retry can really only succeed if we really ran out of space while emitting the small event.
Thanks for the contribution, I added a few comments.

substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.core/src/com/oracle/svm/core/jfr/JfrNativeEventWriter.java
@@ -45,10 +45,10 @@
  * {@link JfrNativeEventWriter}s are finished before {@link SubstrateJVM#endRecording} enters the
  * safepoint.
  *
- * A JFR event writer pre-allocates a size field for an event, {@link java.lang.Byte.BYTES} byte for a small event
- * and {@link java.lang.Integer.BYTES} bytes for a large event. If an event was written as a small event, but actual
+ * A JFR event writer pre-allocates a size field for an event, {@link java.lang.Byte#BYTES} byte for a small event
+ * and {@link java.lang.Integer#BYTES} bytes for a large event. If an event was written as a small event, but actual
  * size exceeds pre-allocated size, a retry should be employed to write the event as a large event. See
- * {@link EndChunkNativePeriodicEvents#emitJVMInformation} for an example.
+ * {@link com.oracle.svm.core.jfr.events.EndChunkNativePeriodicEvents#emitJVMInformation} for an example.
  */
 @DuplicatedInNativeCode
 public final class JfrNativeEventWriter {
